pr_body:
PR for Big HTTP Download - Upgrade 

The PR #26719 must be closed. All updates to code reviews were moved here also.

Fixes #26717
pr_comments:
Form @pfalcon in #26719: 
Thanks for the patches. They definitely make this sample more complicated, but I'm not sure they improve it. Please keep in mind that this a sample, not a wget implementation or something. Its purpose is to show that it's possible to write simple, POSIX-compatible applications for Zephyr. Specifically:

This sample should be simple for user to study (the less code the better, or at least "more code" is not an improvement).
This sample should be simple, and small, and thus run on as many device as possible (usage of floating-point arithmetic is specifically avoided).
This sample should be buildable on a standard POSIX system (e.g. Linux) using make -f Makefile.posix, and this should be achieved with as few #ifdef's in the source code as possible (so, adding more isn't a good direction).
I think that this patch in its current shape deteriorates the sample on all the points above.

Looking just at the functionality, I agree that showing download speed would be useful. As I mentioned elsewhere, the reason I didn't add it myself is, well, because the figures which come out aren't exactly to brag about :-I. And then, there're multiple download speeds - e.g. averaged over all iterations, averaged over the current iteration, instantaneous (i.e. averaged over small period of time, 3-5s). IMHO, the most useful for Zephyr testing would be the last.

Hey @pfalcon thank you for your answer.

> 
> This sample should be simple for user to study (the less code the better, or at least "more code" is not an improvement).

- Why showing KiB and MiB makes the sample complicated? There are only three additional defines and some couple of strings needed.

- I agree with it. Floating point arithmetic were removed.
- The sample is also a way far from being `wget` ;)
> This sample should be buildable on a standard POSIX system (e.g. Linux) using make -f Makefile.posix, and this should be achieved with as few #ifdef's in the source code as possible (so, adding more isn't a good direction).

- Currently POSIX is not possible to compile due to absence of the header `mbedtls/md.h`. Please try to compile for POSIX.
- Why so scary about `#ifdef's`?

> I think that this patch in its current shape deteriorates the sample on all the points above.

- I do not agree: see my explanations above and the less amount of code needed for my improvements.
> 
> Looking just at the functionality, I agree that showing download speed would be useful. As I mentioned elsewhere, the reason I didn't add it myself is, well, because the figures which come out aren't exactly to brag about :-I. And then, there're multiple download speeds - e.g. averaged over all iterations, averaged over the current iteration, instantaneous (i.e. averaged over small period of time, 3-5s). IMHO, the most useful for Zephyr testing would be the last.

Ok. Then I can add the averaged speed.

If you completely disagree with my improvements, please write it here and I will not invest my time in this upgrade anymore. Otherway please test the improved sample and give me a feedback/review on needed changes.

> samples: net: sockets: big_http_download: add progress metrics 

I don't think this commit message correctly describes the change. The matter, the was progress metrics already. You added more to them, or extended them, then please write just that: "samples: net: sockets: big_http_download: Extend progress metrics".

> > samples: net: sockets: big_http_download: add progress metrics 
> 
> I don't think this commit message correctly describes the change. The matter, the was progress metrics already. You added more to them, or extended them, then please write just that: "samples: net: sockets: big_http_download: Extend progress metrics".

Ok. Will do it.
Dear all. With this push I kept the changes as small as possible and also improved all suggested parts. For me the upgrade looks very good now. I hope you enjoy the possible last review :D

issue_context.title: Big HTTP Download - Upgrade
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**

- [Big HTTP Download](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/samples/net/sockets/big_http_download/README.html) example does not prints useful metrics (KiB, MiB, KiB/sec.) of download progress. It leads to time waste at development.

- [Big HTTP Download](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/samples/net/sockets/big_http_download/README.html) example does not supports [Zephyr logging API](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/reference/logging/index.html) properly. It leads to lost debug messages at dev time.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The example project should become above upgrades.
comments:
> does not prints useful metrics (KiB, MiB, KiB/sec.) of download progress. It leads to time waste at development.

Can you elaborate, what you mean by this? (The last sentence specifically).

> > does not prints useful metrics (KiB, MiB, KiB/sec.) of download progress. It leads to time waste at development.
> 
> Can you elaborate, what you mean by this? (The last sentence specifically).

I mean downloaded [`Kibibytes aka KiB`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibibyte), `Mibibytes aka MiB`. Currently only Bytes will be printed - it is kind a hard to read.

review_comments: from @pfalcon in #26719 : I'm not sure about usage of floating-point arithmetic. This would be one cause of stack usage growth you faced. And it would grow binary size, and potentially make it not fit on smaller devices, which would be a loss of functionality.
Will be changed to int arithmetics within next push.
